full_dataset_size: Repo itself: ~150 KB of source, the only committed data is the 24-row placeholder schedule.ts (5.9 KB) plus data/teams (~117 KB squads). Upstream openfootball/worldcup.json 2026/ folder: 7 files, ~740 KB (worldcup.json 43 KB 104 matches, worldcup-full.json 288 KB, squads 385 KB, teams 12 KB, groups 2 KB, stadiums 3 KB, quali_playoffs 6 KB); no compression needed.
description: Complete FIFA World Cup 2026 fixture list: one row per match (104 matches, 48 teams, 16 host cities in the US, Canada and Mexico, 11 Jun-19 Jul 2026) with round/group, local kickoff time and UTC, teams, venue city and full-time score, plus a 16-row stadium table with capacity, country and coordinates. The catalogued repo is an MIT Next.js calendar site whose committed schedule is a placeholder; its ICS feed is rendered at request time from the CC0 openfootball/worldcup.json feed, which is the actual data source and was sampled here. An analyst would join match dates x host city to Inside Airbnb calendar/reviews panels (LA, NYC, Mexico City, Toronto, Miami, etc.) to build city-day event dummies for the 3Q26 nights nowcast, size the NA/LatAm regional mix shock, and use stadium capacity as an intensity weight.
issues: Job card says 64 matches; the 2026 format is 104 matches (48 teams) and the sample has all 104. The repo's own committed schedule.ts is a 24-row placeholder with wrong kickoff times (e.g. Mexico-South Africa listed 23:00Z vs actual 19:00Z) and only 13 cities; do not use it, use the openfootball CSV. The 'auto-updating iCal feed' is a runtime API route (app/api/calendar), not a committed file, so no .ics was pulled; generateIcs.ts shows how to render one. Coordinates in stadiums file mix DMS and decimal formats and were read with a degree-sign encoding artefact in the console (file bytes are fine, UTF-8). Licences: repo MIT, upstream openfootball CC0-1.0 -- no concerns. Team-name spellings differ between the two sources (Korea Republic vs South Korea, Czechia vs Czech Republic).
